Fed Officials Signal More Interest-Rate Increases Ahead, and Markets Believe It

en.title: Fed Officials Signal More Rate Hikes Ahead
en.dek: Fed presidents Musalem and Logan said additional hikes are likely, prompting market expectations of tightening.
facts: According to CNBC, Musalem said another rate hike will be needed soon.
According to CNBC, Logan predicted at least two more 25‑basis‑point increases.
CME’s FedWatch tool priced a 76% likelihood of a 25‑basis‑point hike in December.
According to MarketWatch, Logan sees at least 50 basis points in future hikes.
body: On 30 October 2026, two Federal Reserve presidents signaled that more rate hikes are likely. According to CNBC, Musalem said another hike would be needed soon, and Logan predicted at least two more 25‑basis‑point increases. The comments came after the Fed left rates unchanged on Wednesday.

Musalem said inflation is too high. He added that core inflation is being closely watched, and that the economy remains resilient with a 3.4% GDP growth. He also noted that the labor market is stable with a 4.2% unemployment rate.

Logan said the Fed needs at least two more 25‑basis‑point hikes. She added that the Fed could skip a meeting, and that a pause would allow the economy to adapt. She will vote on the December decision, while Musalem is a non‑voting member until 2028.

CME’s FedWatch tool priced a 76% chance of a 25‑basis‑point hike in December, while MarketWatch reported that Logan sees at least 50 basis points in future hikes, and Barron's noted that markets believe the Fed will raise rates again.
en.context: According to CNBC, the Fed left rates unchanged on Wednesday, but officials said more hikes are likely.
